//: Peer applications Carlos may call, and what each call does to the world.
//policy: No addresses here. Each peer names an environment variable that holds its
base URL, so this file is identical on every machine and a peer nobody has
configured reports as unresolved rather than being guessed at.
side_effect is required per endpoint and is a reviewed fact, not a comment:
none = a read, persists = writes to existing state, creates = makes something.
These entries are stubs describing intended integrations. Nothing here sends
a request in this build - see src/interop.py.

peers.description: A store that keeps named patches. The persistence Carlos deliberately does not implement itself while the datastore question is open.

endpoints.name: publish
endpoints.description: Deposit a whole patch document as it stands.

endpoints.name: index
endpoints.description: Update a searchable index with counts only, no topology.

peers.description: A tool that draws stage and rack diagrams. Wants the routing, not the sound.

endpoints.name: render
endpoints.description: One readable line per cable, which is what a plot is.

peers.description: An inventory that tracks which devices a rig calls for.

endpoints.name: reconcile
endpoints.description: Distinct devices by catalogue id, so the other side can match on the same addressing scheme.

endpoints.name: check
endpoints.description: Ask what is missing without changing anything.
